beliefs: f strips all leading and trailing whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines) from the input [E2, E8, E16, E21, E23, E24]
After whitespace stripping, f strips the first character iff it is 'H' and the remaining string has length >= 2, regardless of the second character [E6, E11, E21, E22, E23, E24]
The H-strip applies to 'H' followed by lowercase, digit, space, symbol, or uppercase [E6, E11, E22]
Single 'H' alone (after whitespace strip) returns empty string [E21, E22, E24]
Strings starting with any other uppercase letter (A,B,C,D,E,F,G,I,J,K,L,M,N,O,P,Q,R,S,T,U,V,W,X,Y,Z) are returned unchanged after whitespace strip [E10, E14, E15, E17, E18, E19, E20]
Strings starting with lowercase or digit are returned unchanged after whitespace strip [E2, E8, E19]
Empty strings and all-whitespace strings return empty after whitespace strip [E1, E8, E21, E23, E24]
notes: E24 shows f strips tabs and newlines too, not just ASCII spaces, so I switched strip(' ') to strip() (Python's default whitespace strip). The H-strip rule is unchanged and now applies after full whitespace stripping, e.g. '\tHbc' -> 'bc' and '\tH' -> ''.
